title: Chicken or Turkey with Cream Sauce

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey with cream sauce is tender poultry meat sautéed and simmered in a rich sauce made from cream, butter, and seasonings. The dish offers a smooth, buttery flavor and aromatic herbs, suitable for everyday meals or special occasions.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cream sauce is often deglazed with white wine or broth to deepen the flavor.
Traditionally served over pasta, rice, or mashed potatoes.
Turkey is leaner than chicken, but both provide high-quality protein.
Cream gives the sauce a velvety texture and helps retain moisture in the meat.
Some regional variations add mushrooms or a touch of mustard for extra complexity.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken and turkey supply high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Poultry is abundant in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, supporting metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Calcium from cream
items.content: The creamy sauce adds calcium, important for bone health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The dish fits low‑carb diets when paired with non‑starchy sides.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: Cream contains monounsaturated fats that can be heart‑friendly in moderation.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: The cream sauce may trigger reactions in people sensitive to milk proteins or lactose.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Cream and butter increase the dish’s calorie density; portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Using prepared broths or soy sauces can raise the sodium content.

items.title: Proper cooking
items.content: Poultry must be cooked thoroughly to eliminate the risk of salmonella.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Sauté chicken or turkey pieces until golden, then add onion, garlic, and herbs. Pour in cream (or a cream‑broth mix), bring to a simmer, and cook on low heat 15–20 minutes until the meat is tender. Optional additions include mushrooms, fresh parsley, or a sprinkle of grated Parmesan.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer keeping, freeze the cooled dish in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months.
